subject: Onboarding burn-rate alignment and acceptance gates
messages:
From: Emily Turner <emily.turner@atlashealth.com>
To: neha_kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>
Cc: Rajesh Iyer <rajesh.iyer@atlashealth.com>, ben_carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 20 Oct 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Onboarding plan and target throughput

Neha,

Thanks for the demo last week — the latency profile looks promising. We want to lock in a short MAP so we can start a 60-day eval with defined acceptance gates. Two asks from our side before we kick off: 1) an illustrative monthly token (TPM) ramp you recommend for a pilot that starts at 20M TPM and targets 200M TPM at net-new feature launch, and 2) confirmation of the discount tiers tied to committed TPM.

I attached a rough internal forecast — happy to sync. Ideally we want a 3-month ramp in the MAP with an acceptance gate after month 2 (accuracy on our regression tests) and final acceptance at month 3. Budget owners want clear optics on burn rate and when discounts kick in.

—Emily
Product + Ops, AtlasHealth
From: neha_kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>
To: Emily Turner <emily.turner@atlashealth.com>
Cc: ben_carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, laura_bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 20 Oct 2026 11:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Onboarding plan and target throughput

Emily — thanks, and great to hear the demo hit the mark. Attached is a draft MAP (MAP_v2.xlsx) that outlines a recommended ramp and the milestone-linked pricing. High level:

- Pilot months (Month 0–1): 20M TPM baseline for testing, billed at flex rates with a 10% onboarding credit.
- Ramp months (Month 2–4): 40M -> 100M -> 160M TPM target steps; we recommend committing to month-by-month checkpoints instead of a single cliff to reduce risk.
- Post-acceptance (Month 5+): 200M TPM target with standard committed pricing.

Discount bands in the draft: 5% at 50M TPM sustained for two months, 12% at 150M sustained, and 18% at net-new 200M TPM with a 12-month commit. We can alter the sustain windows if Atlas wants faster crediting.

Two operational notes: the acceptance gate at the end of month 2 should be accuracy/regression on your canonical prompt set (we recommend a locked eval harness). Final acceptance at month 3 (okay to shift to month 4 if you want an extra runway).

Ben, looping you to confirm whether the ramp cadence above needs finance sign-off before we present to Emily's CFO. Laura, please flag any SOW concerns in the redline I sent.

Thanks — Neha
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
From: ben_carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
To: neha_kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>, laura_bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 20 Oct 2026 12:30:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Onboarding plan and target throughput

Neha / Laura — quick read. MAP looks reasonable from pricing ops POV but two things: 1) for Atlas' forecast the sustain windows should be explicit (we suggest "sustained for 60 days" to avoid end-of-month edge cases), and 2) for the 18% tier we need a minimum annual commitment (we propose 6 months minimum at that level otherwise we make the discount retroactive and invoice a catch-up).

I'll draft a short payment cadence appendix for the SOW. Emily — happy to walk through tradeoffs on the sustain windows today if helpful.

—Ben
Sales Operations, Redwood Inference
From: Emily Turner <emily.turner@atlashealth.com>
To: neha_kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>
Cc: Rajesh Iyer <rajesh.iyer@atlashealth.com>, ben_carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 21 Oct 2026 08:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Onboarding plan and target throughput

Thanks Neha and Ben — that framing helps. A few clarifying points from our finance/planning review:

- We can accept a sustained-window approach but need the "sustained for 60 days" to be aligned to the date of first invoice after the threshold is reached (not calendar months).
- For the 18% band, the team requests a 3-month minimum (rather than 6) tied to a ramp guarantee: if we hit 200M in month 3 we will commit to 3 months at that level; if not, we revert to the previous tier with pro-rata billing.
- We want the MAP to include a hard stop: if acceptance gate at month 2 fails, both parties can renegotiate ramp cadence and credits without penalty.

Can you update the draft MAP and SOW with these two changes? We're aiming to finalize the MAP and sign the SOW by Nov 12 so procurement can process billing for December.

—Emily
From: laura_bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
To: Emily Turner <emily.turner@atlashealth.com>, neha_kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>
Cc: ben_carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 22 Oct 2026 10:15:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Onboarding plan and target throughput

Emily — appreciate the clarity. I reviewed the SOW redline and updated two items: 1) the sustain window is now defined as "60 consecutive billing days from the invoice date when the threshold is first exceeded," and 2) the 18% discount is set with a 3-month minimum commitment, with a pro-rata true-up if the 200M level doesn't sustain. I also added the hard stop clause for failed acceptance at month 2 (mutual right to renegotiate without penalty).

I've attached SOW_AtlasHealth_redline.pdf to the thread. If that looks good, Neha can present a final MAP and we can route the SOW to DocuSign. Proposed timeline per Emily's ask: finalize by 2026-11-12.

—Laura
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference
From: neha_kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>
To: Emily Turner <emily.turner@atlashealth.com>
Cc: ben_carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, laura_bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>, Rajesh Iyer <rajesh.iyer@atlashealth.com>
Date: Mon, 8 Nov 2026 17:41:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Onboarding plan and target throughput — final MAP for signoff

Emily / Rajesh — attaching the updated MAP (MAP_v2.xlsx) and the SOW redline as discussed. Summary of changes:

- Ramp cadence: Month 0–1: 20M baseline; Month 2: 40M target (acceptance gate 1 — regression tests); Month 3: 100M target (soft acceptance, monitoring); Month 4: 200M target (final acceptance).
- Discounts: 5% at 50M sustained 60 days; 12% at 150M sustained 60 days; 18% at 200M with a 3-month minimum commitment.
- Acceptance/fallbacks: if acceptance gate at month 2 fails, we enter a 30-day remediation window and both sides can adjust ramp cadence and credits; no automatic penalties.
- Commercial ask: if Atlas agrees to the 3-month minimum at 200M we can provide a one-time onboarding credit equal to 10% of month 1 invoice.

If this aligns, we'll generate the final SOW for signature and route the DocuSign link (included above) to your procurement team. Targeting signature by 2026-11-12 to meet your December billing schedule.

Next step: Emily / Rajesh — reply with approval or small edits and Neha will send the DocuSign packet.

Best — Neha
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

> Attachment stubs: MAP_v2.xlsx (spreadsheet); SOW_AtlasHealth_redline.pdf (PDF)
